title: Incident report: an outdated address on a dispatch label
summary: Báo cáo về nhãn giao hàng dùng địa chỉ cũ, cách nhóm xác định nguyên nhân và điều chỉnh quy trình tạo nhãn.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: On Tuesday morning, a warehouse assistant noticed that a dispatch label showed a customer's previous address. The order screen showed the new address, so she stopped the parcel before it reached the collection trolley. Two similar labels were found during the next hour. All three customers had corrected their delivery details after placing an order, and all three parcels were still in the warehouse. The operations manager asked staff to compare labels with the order screen until the software team understood the problem. This temporary check slowed packing, but it prevented staff from sending parcels using information they already knew was wrong.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The investigation focused on the point when each label was created. The system prepared a label soon after an order entered the packing queue, even if packing would not begin until the following day. When a customer changed an address, the order record was updated, but the prepared label remained unchanged. Staff normally downloaded that label later without seeing when it had been created. The developers reproduced the problem using a test order and two invented addresses. They found no evidence that address changes had failed to save. The disagreement was between a current order record and an older document produced from it.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The team first considered rebuilding every label whenever an address changed. That would make the document more current, but it introduced a difficult situation after a parcel had already left the warehouse. A new label could appear in the system even though the carrier still held the parcel with its original label. Support staff might then believe that the change had reached the carrier. The team therefore separated orders that were waiting for dispatch from orders that had already been collected. For the second group, an address change would require a visible support task rather than an automatic replacement document.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: For parcels still in the warehouse, the chosen design creates the label when a packer requests it. The request uses the delivery address saved at that moment. If the address changes after this step, the packing screen displays a warning beside the label button. The packer must remove the earlier paper label before requesting another one. A short instruction explains this physical action because changing a digital document does not remove a label already attached to a box. The warehouse manager also requested that the screen show the label's creation time, giving staff a useful clue when investigating a disagreement.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Testing included more than the simple example of one changed address. A tester corrected an apartment number, printed a label, and then changed the street name. Another tester opened the same order on two computers to check whether both screens showed the warning. The team also checked an order that had been marked as collected. In that case, the screen created a support task and kept the original dispatch label available for reference. The tests used invented customer details throughout. Warehouse staff tried the new flow with empty boxes, which helped reveal that the instruction about removing paper needed to appear before printing.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The release was introduced to one packing station on Thursday afternoon. A developer and a warehouse supervisor stayed nearby for the first thirty orders. Staff understood the warning, but one packer suggested replacing the phrase 'previous document' with 'old paper label'. The team accepted that wording because it described the object the packer had to remove. Packing time increased slightly during the trial, mainly because staff were reading the new instruction. The supervisor decided to continue until Friday before comparing normal working times. No parcels in the trial required an address correction after collection, so that part still depended on the completed test results.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The final review assigned responsibilities for both prevention and follow-up. The software team would monitor disagreements between label creation times and later address changes. Warehouse supervisors would check that discarded labels went into the confidential paper bin rather than remaining beside a printer. Support would use a separate checklist for parcels already collected, including confirmation of what action the carrier could actually take. The incident was recorded as a document-timing problem, not a failure to save customer details. The team also added a question to future design reviews: when information changes, which prepared documents may still show the earlier version?

title: Workplace procedure: making a shared translation request clear
summary: Quy trình gửi yêu cầu dịch nội bộ, phân biệt người đọc, bản nguồn và phần bắt buộc để tránh làm lại.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Our company now receives translation requests from several departments, but the requests often arrive with different levels of detail. Last month, a translator completed a two-page welcome sheet before learning that the visitors would only receive a small card. The department then asked for a shorter version, and both people repeated work that could have been avoided. This procedure introduces one shared request form for internal translation work. It applies to visitor information, staff announcements, and short event materials. Longer publications will still be discussed separately because their schedules and review needs cannot be explained properly in the same small form.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The person requesting a translation should first describe the reader and the action the reader needs to take. Writing 'for customers' is usually too general. A more useful description might say that first-time visitors need to find the correct entrance and bring their booking reference. The form also asks where the translated text will appear, such as a printed card, a slide, or an email. These details help the translator choose suitable wording and length. Requesters should explain difficult company terms in ordinary language rather than assuming that another department understands them. A short explanation at this stage can prevent several rounds of questions.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Attach one approved source document to the request. Do not send three versions and ask the translator to choose the newest one. The source should already contain the information that the department wants to communicate, including dates and contact details. The requester remains responsible for checking those facts. If some sentences are still waiting for approval, mark them clearly and explain when a decision is expected. Translation can begin on the stable sections, but the request will not be treated as fully ready. This approach allows useful work to start without hiding the uncertainty from the person planning the translation schedule.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The translation coordinator reviews new requests each working morning and replies with an expected delivery date. An urgent label does not automatically move a request ahead of everything else. The requester must explain what will happen if the material arrives later, and the coordinator will compare that consequence with existing commitments. Sometimes the best answer is to translate a smaller section first. For example, an event may need its entrance instructions immediately while the background description can wait. Departments should avoid promising a translated version to an outside audience before the coordinator has confirmed that the requested deadline can be met.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: When the first translation is ready, the department appoints one reviewer to gather comments. Several colleagues may contribute, but they should not send separate sets of instructions directly to the translator. The reviewer checks whether the message is suitable for its purpose and whether names, numbers, and locations remain correct. Preferences about style should be explained with a reason, especially when changing a phrase that is already clear. The translator can then distinguish a necessary correction from an optional preference. If reviewers disagree, the requester should settle the issue before returning the file, rather than asking the translator to resolve a department's internal debate.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Any change to the source after translation begins must be listed in the request record. Sending a replacement attachment with the message 'small updates' is not enough, because the translator would have to compare the whole document to discover them. The requester should identify the changed section and explain whether it replaces or adds information. A new date may require only one correction, while a new reader group may affect the entire text. The coordinator will explain any effect on delivery time before more work continues. Departments can accept the later date or reduce the amount of material they need for the first delivery.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The completed request stays in the shared folder with its source, final translation, and review notes. This record helps colleagues understand why particular wording was chosen when similar material is needed later. It does not mean that an old translation is automatically suitable for a new event. Dates, directions, and reader needs may have changed. During the first month, the coordinator will collect examples of missing information and improve the form where necessary. The aim is to make requests easier to complete, not to add extra steps without a purpose. Departments will receive a short update showing which common misunderstandings the new process has reduced.

title: Service notice: collecting a repaired microwave from the workshop
summary: Thông báo nhận lò vi sóng sau sửa chữa, gồm xác nhận công việc, phương án vận chuyển và kiểm tra phụ kiện.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Thank you for leaving your microwave at Riverside Appliance Workshop. We have completed the agreed repair and will keep the appliance ready for collection from Wednesday morning. This notice explains what was done, what you should bring, and how to arrange transport if you cannot carry it comfortably. Please read the collection details before travelling, because the repair desk and the collection entrance are on different sides of the building. Your collection reference is printed at the top of the attached receipt. Keep that reference available when contacting us so that staff can find your appliance without asking you to repeat its full description.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Your original request concerned a door that did not close reliably. The technician found that the external handle assembly was loose and replaced the agreed part. The repair did not include cosmetic work on the cabinet, so the small scratches noted when you brought the appliance remain. Staff checked the repaired appliance using the workshop's normal completion procedure and recorded the result on the service sheet. You can read that sheet at collection. If you want an explanation of the work, please request it when booking your visit. This gives us time to arrange for the appropriate staff member to be available.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Collections are available between ten in the morning and four in the afternoon on weekdays. Please choose a collection window by replying to our message or calling the workshop. A window lasts thirty minutes, and it helps us bring your appliance from storage before you arrive. It is not a promise that a staff member will be free at an exact minute. If you are running late, call before the window ends so we can decide whether to leave the appliance at the desk or return it to storage. Saturday collection is currently unavailable because the collection area is being used for incoming stock.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Bring your collection reference and the receipt showing the payment already made. The final balance is listed separately on the repair message, so you can check it before your visit. We accept card payment at the desk, but the collection entrance does not have a payment terminal. Please complete payment before taking the appliance outside. If another person is collecting for you, send us their name in advance and give them the reference. They do not need to explain why you cannot attend. However, staff will ask them to confirm which appliance they are collecting, particularly when several similar models are waiting.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: The collection entrance faces the small loading courtyard behind the workshop. There is space for one vehicle beside the door, and the driver should remain nearby while staff bring out the appliance. This space is for loading, not for waiting through the whole collection window. Drivers who arrive early can use the public parking area across the road until their appliance is ready. If you are walking, bring a suitable trolley or another person to help you carry it. Staff can move the appliance to the doorway, but they cannot accompany you to the bus stop or carry it across the road.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: We can arrange a local delivery if collection is difficult. The delivery charge is separate from the repair balance and depends on the destination shown in the booking. Please tell us about stairs or restricted vehicle access before accepting the quote, as these details may affect the arrangement. Our delivery service brings the appliance to the agreed entrance; it does not include placing it on a kitchen shelf. A delivery appointment requires someone to receive the item and check the packaging. If you ask for delivery after reserving a collection window, tell staff to cancel that window so they do not prepare both arrangements.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Before leaving the workshop, compare the appliance and accessories with the intake record. Your rotating plate and support ring are listed there and should leave with the microwave. If anything appears missing, raise the issue while staff can check the storage shelf and repair record together. We will wrap the appliance for transport, but please keep it upright and secure during the journey. At home, follow the manufacturer's instructions when putting it back into use. Keep the service sheet with your receipt in case you need to contact us about this repair. Describe any later concern clearly rather than simply requesting the same repair again.

title: Migration proposal: keeping customer identifiers longer than a screen limit
summary: Đề xuất lưu mã khách hàng đầy đủ thay vì cắt theo giới hạn hiển thị, kèm xử lý dữ liệu cũ và triển khai từng bước.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: The account integration team proposes changing how our application stores identifiers supplied by customer systems. The current field allows twenty characters because the first customer used short identifiers and the original account screen had limited space. Our newest customer uses longer values that include a branch code. During a preparation exercise, staff shortened these values manually so they would fit. Two different accounts then appeared to have the same identifier. No live accounts were merged, but the exercise exposed a risk that cannot be solved by asking each customer to invent a shorter naming system. This proposal concerns storage, display, and the handling of existing values.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The proposed storage field will accept the customer's complete identifier within the new documented limit of eighty characters. That limit covers the examples supplied by our current customers, and future integrations must confirm their requirements before approval. We will not assume that every external system uses the same format. The identifier will remain text, even when it contains only digits, because leading zeroes may be part of the customer's value. Our own internal account number will continue to identify the account inside the application. Keeping these purposes separate allows a customer to revise its reference without changing the identity of our account record.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The screen design needs a separate decision from the storage change. Showing every character in a crowded list would make other useful columns harder to read. The proposal therefore shows a shortened visual preview in the account list while keeping the full value in the account detail panel. A copy button in that panel will copy the complete identifier, not the preview. Search will also use the full stored value. The interface must explain when a displayed value is shortened, because users should not have to guess whether information is missing from storage or simply hidden to keep the page readable.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Existing records require investigation before the migration begins. Some identifiers may already have been shortened outside our application, so increasing the field size will not restore their missing characters. The integration team will compare affected records with files supplied by the relevant customer. Where a complete value can be confirmed, the team will prepare a correction list for review. Where it cannot, the record will remain unchanged and receive a note explaining the uncertainty. We should not construct a longer identifier by combining pieces that merely look plausible. A convincing appearance is not evidence that a reference matches the customer's original account.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: The migration will first run on a copy of the data used for integration testing. Checks will confirm that full identifiers survive import, storage, search, copying, and export. The export check is essential because a longer stored value is not useful if the downloaded file still cuts it short. Test cases will include leading zeroes, branch codes, and two values with the same first twenty characters. The team will also inspect screens that are not part of the main account page, including a small account selector used when creating invoices. This selector may need its own layout adjustment to remain understandable.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: For the first live stage, the larger field will be available only to one integration that has provided complete sample data. Support staff will receive examples of the new display and a guide to checking the full identifier. We will monitor rejected imports and questions about copied values for one week before expanding access. The previous import route will stay available during that period, but it must reject values beyond its limit rather than silently shorten them. If the pilot reveals a serious issue, the team can pause new imports while leaving successfully stored complete values available for investigation and customer reference.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The estimated work is four development days plus time for customer verification, which may vary between integrations. The proposal does not promise to correct every old identifier during the first release. Its immediate goal is to stop the application from treating a display restriction as a rule about customer data. The integration manager will approve correction lists, the product designer will review shortened previews, and support will maintain the explanation used with customers. After the pilot, the team will record any remaining uncertainty and assign owners to it. That record will help later integrations avoid repeating assumptions that were reasonable only for our first customer.

vocabulary.meaning: các chữ số không ở đầu

title: Handover notes: preparing a temporary team leader for daily decisions
summary: Ghi chú bàn giao cho trưởng nhóm tạm thời, làm rõ quyền quyết định, giới hạn công việc và cách hỗ trợ đồng nghiệp.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: I will be away from the office for eight working days, and Mai will act as team leader during that period. These notes cover the decisions she is likely to face rather than listing every task in the department. The team already knows its current assignments, but several pieces of work depend on someone making a choice when circumstances change. My main request is that Mai keeps those decisions visible. A short explanation in the decision log is more useful than a long message sent only to me. I will read the log when I return and should be able to understand what happened without reconstructing private conversations.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Mai can adjust the order of existing tasks when a deadline changes or a colleague is unexpectedly absent. She can also approve small purchases within the team's remaining monthly allowance. She should not accept a new customer commitment that requires extra staffing or changes an agreed delivery date. Those requests go to the department manager, who has the wider view of available people and budgets. If a request is unclear, Mai can ask questions before deciding where it belongs. Sending every question upwards would delay ordinary work, but handling every request alone would place responsibilities on her that this temporary role does not include.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The morning check-in should remain fifteen minutes long. Ask each person what needs attention today and whether another colleague's work is blocking progress. Detailed problem-solving should happen afterwards with the people involved, leaving the rest of the team free to begin work. One customer presentation is scheduled for next Wednesday, and its draft must be ready on Monday afternoon. If the draft is delayed, Mai should arrange a brief review of the available sections rather than cancelling the review completely. An incomplete draft can still reveal a missing explanation or an unrealistic promise before those problems reach the final presentation.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Two colleagues need particular context during this handover. Nam is learning the monthly reporting process and has completed it once with support. He should prepare the next draft himself, then ask Hanh to check the totals and notes before distribution. Taking the task back from him would be quicker today but would remove a useful learning opportunity. Hanh, however, is covering another team's deadline on Thursday and Friday. Mai should therefore arrange the checking time earlier in the week. Both colleagues know this plan, but neither has reserved a time yet. Please make the appointment explicit instead of assuming it will happen naturally.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: The shared inbox contains messages about ongoing work and a few requests that have not yet been accepted. A message being present in the inbox does not mean the team has promised to complete it. Before assigning work from a new message, check the request register for the current status and any earlier discussion. If a customer asks for an update on an unaccepted request, explain that it is still being reviewed and give the next contact date. Do not describe it as late work. This distinction matters because an inaccurate apology can create the impression that the team missed a commitment it never made.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: If two colleagues disagree about a task, Mai should first ask them to identify the practical decision that is needed. A discussion about whose method is better can continue for a long time without clarifying what must happen today. The decision log should record the selected approach, the reason, and any condition that would justify revisiting it. This leaves room for change without keeping the task permanently open. Personal concerns should be discussed privately with the department manager rather than entered in a shared work log. The log is intended to explain operational choices, not to collect opinions about individual colleagues or replace a sensitive conversation.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: On my first morning back, Mai and I will review the log together for twenty minutes. We will focus on unresolved decisions, new commitments approved by the manager, and anything that needs follow-up. Completed routine tasks do not need a separate presentation. I also want to hear whether the authority described in these notes was sufficient. If Mai repeatedly had to wait for approval on ordinary matters, we should improve the next handover rather than treat that delay as her failure. The temporary role should keep work moving and give her supported experience, while leaving a clear record that the whole team can use.

title: Community notice: booking a shared oven for the autumn food fair
summary: Hướng dẫn đặt lò dùng chung cho hội chợ, phối hợp thời gian làm nóng, lấy món và dọn khu vực.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: The neighbourhood centre will make its two kitchen ovens available to residents preparing food for the autumn fair. The aim is to help people who want to contribute but do not have enough oven space at home. This is a booking service for preparing agreed dishes, not an open cooking session where anyone can arrive with ingredients. Residents must reserve a slot and receive confirmation before using the kitchen. The fair committee will display a list of accepted dishes separately. A dish appearing on that list does not automatically include an oven booking, so please complete both arrangements if you need the centre's equipment.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The booking form asks for the dish name, the required oven temperature, and the expected cooking time. It also asks whether the oven needs to be heated before the tray goes in. These details allow the kitchen coordinator to group bookings that use similar temperatures. If the schedule moved repeatedly between very different temperatures, residents would spend much of their slot waiting for the oven to adjust. Please use a cooking time you have already tried rather than choosing an optimistic estimate. If you have never prepared the dish before, discuss the plan with the coordinator before requesting a slot in the busiest period.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Each confirmed booking includes time to place the trays, cook the food, and remove everything from the oven. It does not include preparation of the dish from the beginning. Ingredients should arrive ready for the stage you have booked. The centre has a small work surface, but it must remain available for checking trays and organising the next booking. Residents who need a longer preparation session should make their own arrangements elsewhere. This limit may seem inconvenient, but it prevents one complicated recipe from using the whole kitchen while other people wait with dishes that are ready to go into the oven.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Bring your own trays and mark them with your name using a label that can be removed before cooking. The kitchen coordinator will check that each tray fits the available oven before the booking begins. A photograph alone is not always useful because it may not show the tray's full width. If you are unsure, bring the empty tray to the centre during Thursday's equipment check. The centre will provide oven gloves and a clear space for placing hot trays. Residents should keep bags and coats away from that space so the next person does not have to move personal belongings while carrying a tray.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Please arrive ten minutes before your confirmed slot and report to the kitchen coordinator. You will be told where to wait until the previous booking has finished. If you arrive late, your finishing time will not automatically move later because another resident may be waiting. The coordinator will discuss whether your dish can still fit the remaining time or needs a different slot. Do not place a tray in an oven simply because it looks empty. The oven may be changing temperature for the next booking, and opening the door can interfere with that plan. The coordinator will confirm when it is ready for you.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: When your dish is finished, take your trays to the marked cooling table and clear the work surface you used. The cooling table is shared space, so each booking has one allocated section. It is not a storage area for the rest of the day. Before leaving the kitchen, confirm with a fair volunteer where your dish should go next. Some items will be taken directly to a stall, while others have a separate agreed holding arrangement. Volunteers will use the dish information supplied during registration. If your ingredients have changed, tell the volunteer before the dish is displayed so the information beside it can be corrected.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Residents who no longer need an oven should cancel by Friday lunchtime. This allows the coordinator to offer the slot to someone on the waiting list and adjust the temperature schedule if necessary. On the day, unexpected delays should be reported by phone rather than through the centre's general email inbox. The coordinator will be working in the kitchen and will not check that inbox regularly. After the fair, residents will be invited to comment on the booking system. The committee will consider whether another cooking session is needed next year, but it will base that decision on actual demand and available volunteers rather than the number of dishes alone.

title: Release plan: allowing a colleague to continue a draft request
summary: Kế hoạch cho phép chuyển bản yêu cầu chưa gửi sang đồng nghiệp, với quyền rõ ràng và lịch sử thay đổi.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Our internal purchasing application currently lets employees save an unfinished request, but only its creator can continue editing it. This becomes inconvenient when the creator goes on leave or another colleague needs to finish the item details. Teams have been copying information into a new request or sharing screenshots, which can leave two different drafts describing the same planned purchase. The proposed release adds a way to transfer a draft to a named colleague. It does not submit the request or approve the purchase. The purpose is to let another person continue the preparation while making responsibility for the unfinished document clear.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The creator will open the draft menu and choose 'Transfer draft'. The next screen asks for the receiving colleague and shows the department associated with the request. Only colleagues who already have permission to create requests for that department can receive the draft. If the intended person is not available in the list, the creator will need to ask the department administrator about access. The release will not add permission automatically just because someone has been selected. This avoids making a convenience feature responsible for deciding who may prepare purchases on behalf of a department, which remains a separate organisational decision.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Before confirming, the creator will see a short preview of what moves with the draft. Item descriptions, quantities, attached quotations, and existing preparation notes will transfer together. Personal reminders kept outside the request will stay with the original creator. The preview also warns that the creator will lose editing access after the transfer, although they can still view the record. The team chose one editor at a time because the first release is intended for a clear handover, not simultaneous preparation. The receiving colleague can transfer the draft back later if further work by the original creator becomes necessary.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The receiving colleague will get an application notification containing the draft title and the sender's name. Opening the notification will show the draft and a short handover note written by the sender. That note is required, but it can be brief: for example, it may identify the missing quotation or explain which quantity still needs confirmation. We want recipients to understand the next task without searching through every field. The application will not send an email copy of attached quotations as part of this notification. Those documents remain inside the request, where the existing access rules continue to apply.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: A transfer will be recorded in the request history with the time, sender, recipient, and handover note. Later edits will appear under the name of the person who made them. The history is useful when an approver asks why a quantity or description changed, but it should not imply that the original creator approved the final request. Submission remains a separate action performed by the current editor. On the approval screen, the application will show who submitted the request and provide a link to its history. This should give reviewers context without requiring them to read every change before making an ordinary decision.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Testing will include an ordinary transfer, a transfer back, and an attempt to select a colleague without the necessary department access. The team will also check what happens if access changes between opening the transfer screen and confirming it. In that case, the application must check permission again and explain why the transfer cannot proceed. Another test will use two open browser windows to confirm that the former editor cannot save changes after the transfer succeeds. The draft must remain with its current editor if a transfer fails. An error should not leave the document without anyone able to continue preparing it.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: We will introduce the feature to the facilities department for two weeks before making it available more widely. Their requests often require one person to identify equipment and another to collect quotations, so they can provide useful feedback on the handover note. We will measure completed transfers, failed attempts, and requests for help. A high transfer count alone will not prove success if colleagues still create duplicate drafts afterwards. The review will therefore include a short conversation with users about what happened next. Support guidance will explain the distinction between transferring preparation and approving expenditure, since confusing those actions would weaken the value of the feature.

title: Workplace procedure: arranging a useful second supplier visit
summary: Quy trình tổ chức lần gặp nhà cung cấp thứ hai nhằm giải quyết câu hỏi còn mở, tránh lặp lại buổi giới thiệu.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: The operations department is considering a new supplier for reusable delivery containers. The first visit gave us a general introduction to the product range, but it did not answer several questions about our actual handling process. A second visit has now been proposed. Its purpose is to close those information gaps before we decide whether to run a small trial. It should not become another broad presentation simply because different colleagues attend. This procedure explains how to prepare questions, involve the right people, and record what remains uncertain. A useful visit may lead to a trial, a request for more evidence, or a decision to stop the discussion.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The purchasing coordinator will create a question list from the first visit's notes. Each question should describe a practical situation rather than ask whether the product is generally reliable. For example, we need to know how the containers are checked after returning from a customer and what happens when a damaged lid is found. The list should separate information needed for a trial from information that would only matter during a larger rollout. This distinction keeps the visit focused without pretending that later questions are unimportant. Colleagues should add questions by Tuesday afternoon so the supplier has enough time to bring appropriate examples or records.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Attendance will be based on the questions rather than on department seniority. One warehouse colleague should explain the space available for returned containers, and one delivery colleague should describe how containers are handled during unloading. Purchasing will lead the meeting and record commercial questions. The department manager does not need to attend every demonstration, but should receive the findings before a trial is approved. Keeping the group small makes it easier for people to examine the samples and ask follow-up questions. Anyone unable to attend can submit a specific question and name someone who will check whether it was answered adequately.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The supplier will receive our question list and an outline of the visit in advance. We will ask for two sample containers, including one that has already been used, rather than only new display items. A used sample may show practical features that are difficult to judge from a brochure, such as how clearly its identification mark remains visible. We will also ask the supplier to explain the history of that sample. One object cannot establish how all containers perform, but it can help us ask more precise questions. Staff should record observations separately from the supplier's claims so the final notes do not confuse the two.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: During the visit, the purchasing coordinator will introduce the decision we are trying to make and the time available. Questions about handling and returns will come first because they affect whether a trial is workable at all. Price discussions will follow once the group understands what service and replacement arrangements the quotation includes. If a question cannot be answered immediately, record the missing information and agree who will supply it by what date. Avoid filling the gap with an assumption just to complete the notes. A visible unanswered question is more useful than a confident statement that neither side has actually confirmed.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: After the supplier leaves, the group will spend fifteen minutes comparing its observations. Each person should identify one advantage, one concern, and any question that remains open. Differences in opinion should be connected to the person's working conditions. A container that seems easy to lift in the meeting room may still be awkward in the limited space beside a delivery vehicle. The summary should therefore explain the context of a concern rather than label the product simply good or bad. Purchasing will send the supplier a factual follow-up list, but internal preferences about competing suppliers will stay in our own decision record.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The final recommendation must state whether the available information supports a small trial and what that trial would need to test. If the group recommends proceeding, it should propose the number of containers, the location, and the person responsible for collecting results. If an important question remains unanswered, the recommendation may be to wait. There is no requirement to reward a second visit with an order. The supplier's time should be respected through clear preparation and prompt follow-up, while our decision should depend on evidence relevant to our work. The coordinator will keep the visit record so later negotiations can refer to the same confirmed information.

title: Transport notice: checking in for a train journey with a folding bicycle
summary: Thông báo hư cấu về hành trình tàu có xe đạp gấp, giải thích đặt chỗ, kích thước gói và đổi phương án khi cần.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: From next month, North Valley Rail will trial a reserved luggage area for passengers travelling with folding bicycles on selected weekend services. The trial responds to requests from people who cycle to a station but want to complete the longer part of their journey by train. Space is limited, so a normal passenger ticket will not by itself reserve room for a bicycle. This notice explains the trial arrangements for the listed services only. Other trains will continue to use their existing luggage procedures. Please check that both your outward and return services are included before planning a trip that depends on the new arrangement.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Passengers should reserve a bicycle space when buying their ticket or add one later through the booking desk. The reservation applies to a folded bicycle in a travel cover, not to a full-size bicycle rolled onto the train. The booking page gives the maximum package dimensions for the trial luggage area. Measure your bicycle after folding and covering it, including any parts that extend beyond the main frame. A bicycle described by its manufacturer as compact may still be too large for this particular space. If you are unsure about the measurement, contact the booking desk before paying for a journey you cannot comfortably make.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: At the station, report to the assistance point twenty minutes before departure. Staff will check your bicycle reservation and direct you to the correct carriage. The bicycle should already be folded and covered when you reach the assistance point, as this area is also used by passengers asking for directions. Do not leave the work of folding it until the train is ready to depart. Staff can explain the loading route, but passengers are responsible for moving their own bicycles. If you need help, arrange a companion or discuss the available station assistance in advance rather than assuming that a staff member can carry the package.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The reserved area is beside the luggage shelves in the rear carriage. Each bicycle reservation has a marked position, which staff will identify during boarding. Put the covered bicycle in that position and keep smaller bags with you unless another luggage space is available. The bicycle cover should contain loose straps so they do not extend into the walking route. A reserved position does not give a passenger use of the entire luggage area. Other passengers may still need to place ordinary suitcases on the nearby shelves. Please follow staff instructions if items need to be moved to keep the aisle clear.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: If you change to a different train, your bicycle reservation must be checked separately from your passenger ticket. A seat being available does not mean that a bicycle position is available too. The booking desk can explain the options before confirming the change. You may be offered a later service in the trial, or you may decide to travel without the bicycle. Do not board an unlisted service expecting staff to create an extra position. If the railway changes your service, staff will contact you using the details in your booking and explain the available arrangements for both the passenger and the bicycle.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Before arrival, check the announcement about which side of the train will open. Keep the bicycle folded until you have left the platform and reached an area where unfolding it will not block other passengers. At Hill Market station, that area is the paved space beyond the main exit. The station has a narrow platform, so passengers should not stop there to adjust bicycle parts or attach bags. If you are meeting someone, ask them to wait outside the exit rather than beside the carriage door. This gives people leaving the train room to move and prevents the luggage area from becoming a meeting point.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The trial will run for six weekends, after which the railway will review demand and staff reports. Feedback will ask about booking clarity, loading time, and the usefulness of the marked positions. The review will also consider passengers who could not obtain a reservation, since a service may be useful even when its spaces fill quickly. An extension has not yet been agreed. Existing reservations for the published trial dates will remain valid, but passengers should wait for an announcement before planning later journeys around the same arrangement. Our aim is to learn whether the available space can support a predictable service for cyclists and other passengers together.

title: Support investigation: a copied link opening the wrong workspace
summary: Điều tra liên kết công việc mở sai không gian làm việc, phân biệt lỗi định tuyến với mất dữ liệu và thiết kế thông báo phù hợp.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: A customer contacted support after a colleague sent her a link to a maintenance task. When she opened it, the application displayed a different task with a similar number. She worked in two workspaces belonging to the same organisation, and the application opened the link in the workspace she had used most recently. The customer was concerned that the original task had been replaced. Support asked her not to edit the displayed task while the issue was investigated. They also requested the copied link and the name of the workspace where the sender had found the intended task, avoiding a conclusion based only on the similar numbers.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The support engineer found that the copied link contained a task number but no workspace reference. Task numbers were unique within each workspace, rather than across the entire application. The link handler therefore looked for that number in whichever workspace was currently active. In this customer's case, both workspaces contained a task with that number, so the application opened a valid record in the wrong context instead of showing an error. The original maintenance task remained unchanged in its own workspace. The engineer reproduced the behaviour with two test workspaces and recorded the sequence so the development team could examine the routing decision.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The immediate support response explained the difference between a missing task and a link that lacked enough context. The customer was asked to select the intended workspace before opening the old link again. This was a temporary workaround, not the proposed long-term solution, because users should not need to remember the sender's active workspace. Support also checked whether the recipient already had access to the intended workspace. She did, so no permission change was required. The team avoided describing the issue as lost data, since that explanation would have caused unnecessary concern and did not match what the investigation had found.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The development proposal adds a workspace reference to links created by the task page. When a recipient opens a new link, the application will use that reference to locate the task before deciding what to display. The reference will not grant access on its own. If the recipient lacks permission, the application will explain that the task belongs to another workspace and offer the existing access-request route. It will not switch silently to a different task with the same number. This distinction matters because a precise destination and permission to view that destination are separate requirements, even when they appear together in a single link.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Older links need different handling because their missing workspace cannot always be recovered from the URL. The team considered choosing the first matching task, but rejected that approach because the order of search results would not establish the sender's intention. Instead, an older link will ask the user to select a workspace before continuing. The selection screen will explain why the question is necessary and show only workspaces the user can access. If no matching task exists in the selected workspace, the application will show a clear message and let the user try another workspace. It will not automatically continue searching and open an unexpected result.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Testing will cover new and old links, users with one workspace, and users with several. One case will deliberately create the same task number in two workspaces, then open a new link while the other workspace is active. Another will remove the recipient's access after the link has been copied. The expected result is an access message, not a substitute task. Tests will also check a task that has been deleted from the correct workspace. Support requested that this message differ from the access message, because users need to know whether they should contact a workspace administrator or ask the sender for a current task link.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The fix will be released first to the affected organisation and two internal test teams. Support will follow up with the original customer to confirm that new copied links reach the intended task from either active workspace. The team will also review questions caused by the selection screen for older links. Some extra explanation may be needed, but opening a question screen is preferable to quietly opening an unrelated record. Once the behaviour is confirmed, the documentation will show examples of both link formats. Future reviews of shared links will check whether the destination contains enough context, rather than assuming that a number identifies the same object everywhere.
